**Amazon for Clinical Trials + Consumer Reports for Drugs**

[A decentralized framework for drug assessment (dFDA)](/knowledge/solution/dfda-academic.qmd) achieves **{{< var trial_cost_reduction_factor >}}x cost reduction** through decentralized pragmatic trials.
Patients can search treatments ranked by real-world effectiveness and join trials with one click.

#### Safety Assessment vs Current Standards

**Current FDA system:**

- Adverse events require filling out a PDF form (seriously)
- Most side effects never get reported
- No public database of outcome frequencies
- Society finds out a drug causes heart attacks 10 years later when lawyers get involved

**A decentralized assessment system:**

- Adverse events collected automatically from every participant
- Real-time reporting to everyone (not buried in FDA databases)
- Outcome labels show exact frequency and severity of every effect
- Patients know the risks BEFORE taking the drug, not after the class action lawsuit

The FDA does not publish adverse event rates. They make people guess. The framework shows: "12% of patients got headaches, 3% were severe, 0.1% discontinued treatment." That's not less safe than the current system. That's actually having safety data.

#### Treatment Rankings

Comparative Effectiveness

**Current system:** Doctors pick treatments based on:

- The drug rep who brought good donuts in 2003
- Concepts half-remembered from medical school
- Whatever the insurance company allows
- Vibes

[A decentralized framework for drug assessment](/knowledge/solution/dfda-academic.qmd): Patients enter a condition and see every [treatment ranked by real-world effectiveness](/knowledge/solution/dfda-academic.qmd):

![Treatment Rankings Example](/assets/dfda-comparative-effectiveness-ranking-search.png)

Rankings are based on frequency and magnitude of health outcome changes across all patients - or filtered to patients with similar omic profiles. A treatment that works great for 25-year-old women with specific genetic variants might not work for 60-year-old men with different variants. The framework shows what works for similar people, not average effects across everyone.

##### Outcome Labels

*Standardized Outcome Summaries*

Food has nutrition labels.
Cigarettes have warning labels.
Drugs have... incomprehensible 40-page inserts written by lawyers having seizures.

[A decentralized framework for drug assessment](/knowledge/solution/dfda-academic.qmd) fixes that with **[Outcome Labels](/knowledge/solution/dfda-academic.qmd)** - simple, data-driven summaries showing exactly what happens when real people try a treatment:

![Outcome Labels Example](/assets/dfda-outcome-labels.png)

Based on thousands of real patients, the data shows:

- **Cognitive Improvements**: Memory +35%, Executive Function +22%
- **Side Effects**: Headache +9% (mild), Fatigue +7% (moderate)
- **Discontinuation rate**: 2.3% stopped due to side effects
- **The Truth**: Not marketing claims, actual measured effects from real humans

No more pharmaceutical fan fiction.
No more lawyers writing medical advice during fever dreams.
Just cold, hard data about whether this chemical makes human meat work better or worse.
